meta.title: The Population Race 1800–2100 | India Overtakes China, Nigeria Rises
meta.shorts_title: 300 years of the population race in 2 minutes
meta.description: In 1800, 54% of the world's 1 billion people lived in China and India. This bar-chart race shows the 10 most populous countries from 1800 to 2100, using Gapminder data and UN projections for the future. Watch the USA climb to #3, India overtake China, and Pakistan, Nigeria and DR Congo surge up the table.
meta.sources_long: Gapminder Population v8 (based on UN World Population Prospects), via github.com/open-numbers/ddf--gapminder--fasttrack
meta.pinned_comment: Which surprised you more: Pakistan passing the USA, or China falling below 1 billion?

captions.text: About 1 billion people on Earth, and 54% of them live in just two countries: China and India (today's borders).
Europe's industrial age: 5 European countries make the top 10.
Waves of immigration push the USA up to #3. It still holds that spot today.
2.5 billion people. Vaccines, antibiotics and better food are about to change everything.
China introduces its one-child policy. Watch the gap with India start to close.
Pakistan and Nigeria are climbing fast. Keep an eye on them.
India overtakes China to become the most populous country on Earth.
UN projections. The future isn't fixed, but the trend is strong.
Pakistan passes the USA. Nigeria follows in 2057.
India peaks at about 1.70 billion, then starts to shrink.
China falls below 1 billion, from a peak of 1.43 billion in 2021.
Three of today's fastest-growing nations, Pakistan, Nigeria and DR Congo, sit in the top 5.
